messages:
Maya Singh: heads-up — found an odd routing case where a GET /v1/projects?org_id=<orgA> returned a project owned by orgB. reproducer attached. @sam can you take a look? :thinking:
Sam Ortiz: ack. can you paste the exact request/response?
Maya Singh: copied from local repro (sanitized):
```
GET /v1/projects?org_id=orgA HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer token-user-123

200 OK
[
  {"project_id":"p-842","org_id":"orgB","name":"shared-utils"}
]
```
Maya Singh: audit shows user-agent=service-x, request originated from routing-gateway-2. audit log entry: `audit.log: ts=2026-03-19T15:04:12Z user=user-123 action=list_projects params={org_id:orgA} result_count=3`
Eli Nguyen: that's not great. quick hypothesis — we recently changed the routing table to prefer region-local backends and the project-list handler does a workspace->org resolution via project routing keys. maybe a cache key drop caused project metadata from orgB to be returned for orgA queries.
Rachel K: also saw a KMS binding that looked odd in prod earlier today. `kms_bindings:list --key=projects/orgA/key` returned an entry referencing `project: p-842` which is orgB-owned. possible stale KMS policy?
Sam Ortiz: can we confirm whether the KMS binding is the source or just a symptom? eli, can you run a quick diff of project->org index vs routing table for p-842?
Eli Nguyen: running queries now. quick logs: `indexer: lookup project p-842 -> owner_org=orgB`, `router: cache lookup key=project_meta:p-842 -> value belongs_to=orgB`, but when serving list_projects(orgA) the shard merge included a partial result from shard-7 which returned p-842. shard-7 was in maintenance window and restarted ~15m before incident window.
Maya Singh: reproduction on staging with routing-gateway-2 + cache priming shows same ordering where stale shard returns artifact. looks like we lacked an org filter after merge. code snippet from merge function: 
```
// simplified
merged := append(resultsFromShards...)
return merged
```
no explicit org_id check after merging.
Sam Ortiz: oof. that's a logic hole — we rely on upstream shards to filter but can't trust that during restarts. mitigation: add server-side guard: filter merged list by requested org_id before returning. quick patch and hotfix?
Rachel K: agree. also revoke any KMS bindings that reference cross-org projects while we triage. I'll start a scoped revoke for bindings that don't match owner_org.
Maya Singh: @infra-bot can you cordon shard-7 from the router pool while we patch?
infra-bot: Action queued — cordon shard-7. Expected completion: 30s. :wrench:
Sam Ortiz: I'll open a PR with the filter + unit test, push to canary, and roll to prod once green. target: 30m. PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1123 (will notify here).
Eli Nguyen: add an audit-alert: create a rule to flag list_projects responses that include projects with owner_org != requested org_id. sec-oncall-bot should page on 2 matches in 5m.
sec-oncall-bot: Alert rule created: `cross_org_project_in_list` scope=prod threshold=2/5m. Pager: oncall@redwood.com
Maya Singh: filing incident ticket INF-4527. summary: "Project list merge returned cross-org artifact due to lack of post-merge org filter; KMS binding surfaced as symptom."
Rachel K: good. I'll draft a short customer-facing blurb in #security-comms if this hits any external accounts. so far no PII/lateral access detected, just visibility of project metadata.
Sam Ortiz: rolled canary patch -> canary logs show zero cross-org items on canary routers. deploying to prod now.
Maya Singh: after prod deploy, run a full scan for any projects returned to orgs that don't own them and revoke any suspicious KMS bindings. put findings in INF-4527.
Eli Nguyen: noted. follow-up actions: 1) hotfix filter (done), 2) add unit/integration tests for merge path, 3) add post-merge sanity check, 4) audit KMS bindings and revoke mismatches, 5) postmortem if confirmed leak >1 affected orgs.
Maya Singh: thanks team. keeping channel updated. :thumbsup:
